hook: The weekend lie-in is not recovering your sleep debt. It's shifting your internal clock forward — and it's making Monday measurably harder than it needs to be.
topic: Social jet lag — why variable sleep timing is its own form of impairment
body:
**If you sleep at midnight and wake at 8am on weekdays, then stay up until 2am and wake at 10am on weekends — you have just given yourself the equivalent of a two-hour jet lag every Monday morning. Without getting on a plane.**

This is called social jet lag, and it is one of the most consistently documented and consistently ignored sources of cognitive impairment in the working population.

Here's the mechanism. Your circadian clock anchors itself to your sleep and wake times. When you shift those times by two or more hours on the weekend, the clock recalibrates to the later schedule. Monday morning, you are waking two hours before your biological clock says it's time. Cortisol hasn't risen appropriately. Melatonin clearance is incomplete. You are physiologically in the middle of the night while your alarm tells you it's morning.

The lie-in doesn't pay off the debt. It moves the debt forward and charges a timing penalty on top.

The highest-leverage sleep intervention most people aren't using: a consistent wake time, seven days a week. Even when you've slept badly. Especially then.

More detail on the mechanism — link in bio.
